doc.title: Virginia Mayhew interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 23, 2022

chapter: Working with Al Grey and Diva
title: State Department jazz ambassador tours
summary: She toured twice for the State Department, including Central Asia and Laos, sitting in with a khene player; trio and quartet lineups.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: I understand that you’ve been like a jazz ambassador to some other countries?

I’ve done that twice for the State Department and what an amazing experience that was. They send you to someplace sort of off the beaten track. And the first time we went to the newly independent states like Kazakhstan and Moldova, Ukraine, all these places that haven’t really experienced jazz except in a lot of these places they have. There’ll be like a little contingent of people that love jazz and you know, play, and something like that. And then there’ll be all these people that have no idea. But I think it’s a really important thing for the United States to send around good will ambassadors like that. And they told us clearly do not talk about politics, but it was — [to off camera 41:01 888] are you almost finished? It was a great experience and I met a lot of people that were — well not a lot but I met some people that played different instruments and they were great musicians, like something called — I think it was called a khene in Laos. I think it was called a ken — k-e-n. And we did something at this little school and this guy sat in, or they played for us, and he was playing some sort of drum thing with — by hand — all sorts of little things. And so we invited him to sit in on a gig. So he brought that and then he also brought this khene thing, which is some sort of bamboo thing. And we started playing a minor blues and he said yeah, yeah. And he played the heck out of that thing. And it was just the most amazing, amazing thing.
Well that comes from a long line of illustrious ambassadors starting with Louis Armstrong and
Yeah, it was a great honor to do that twice.

Yup. The first time it was a trio, Allison Miller and Gary Wang. And the next time it was a quartet with — who did I take — Harvie S., Allison Miller and Daniel Kelley on piano. It was just — that was bossa nova. The first one the theme was Louis Armstrong, the second one the theme was bossa nova, or something, what was it — I think it was bossa nova or something like that. And it was just really, it was so much fun and people just loved it and it was just such an amazing experience to see all these off-the-beaten-path places.
